questions.answer: Density is mass per unit volume; ρ = m/V.
accepted_alternatives: the mass of a substance divided by its volume
questions.unit_policy: No numerical unit is required; the equation must identify mass divided by volume.

marking_points.text: States that density is mass per unit volume
Writes ρ = m/V or an equivalent word equation
Identifies pressure as normal force per unit area

option_feedback.A: Correct. Pressure is normal force per unit area.
option_feedback.B: A force parallel to the surface does not press the two surfaces together.
option_feedback.C: Pressure divides normal force by area; it does not multiply them.
option_feedback.D: Mass per unit area is not pressure and does not include a force.

questions.unit_policy: No unit is required because the response is a ratio.

marking_points.text: Infers that reducing area from 0.040 m² to 0.010 m² makes the pressure four times as large

option_feedback.A: This reverses the inverse relation. The smaller area produces greater pressure.
option_feedback.B: The normal force is unchanged, but the contact area is not.
option_feedback.C: Correct. The area becomes one quarter, so F/A becomes four times as large.
option_feedback.D: Sixteen would come from applying the area factor twice. The areas are already given in m².

questions.unit_policy: The selected force is measured in newtons.

marking_points.text: Uses vertical equilibrium to identify the floor normal force as 500 - 80 = 420 N

option_feedback.A: 80 N is the upward handle force, not the downward force exerted on the floor.
option_feedback.B: Correct. The upward handle force reduces the floor normal force to 420 N.
option_feedback.C: 500 N is the weight, but the handle supports 80 N of it.
option_feedback.D: Adding the upward handle force to the weight gives the wrong direction for equilibrium.

accepted_alternatives: Area 96.0 mm² followed by a correct conversion to 9.60 × 10⁻⁵ m²
questions.unit_policy: Area must be stated in m², pressure in Pa, and the converted pressure in MPa.
questions.tolerance: Accept 9.6 × 10⁻⁵ m² and pressure values consistent with 5.0 × 10⁶ Pa to at least two significant figures.

marking_points.text: Converts both contact dimensions to metres and obtains area 9.60 × 10⁻⁵ m²
Uses p = F/A with F = 480 N and the converted contact area
Obtains pressure 5.00 × 10⁶ Pa
Converts 5.00 × 10⁶ Pa to 5.00 MPa

questions.answer: One foot has area (0.030)(0.020) = 6.0 × 10⁻⁴ m², so four feet have total area 2.4 × 10⁻³ m². Vertical equilibrium gives N + 180 = 900, hence N = 720 N. p = 720/(2.4 × 10⁻³) = 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa. The upward strap supports 180 N of the weight, so the floor carries only 720 N.
accepted_alternatives: 0.0024 m² for total area and 300 kPa for pressure
questions.unit_policy: Contact area must be in m², normal force in N and pressure in Pa or an exactly equivalent prefixed SI unit.
questions.tolerance: Accept results consistent with 2.4 × 10⁻³ m², 720 N and 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa to two significant figures.

marking_points.text: Converts 3.0 cm by 2.0 cm to one-foot area 6.0 × 10⁻⁴ m²
Uses all four feet to obtain total contact area 2.4 × 10⁻³ m²
Uses vertical equilibrium to obtain normal force 900 - 180 = 720 N
Uses p = F/A with the 720 N normal force and total contact area
Obtains uniform pressure 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa
Explains that the upward 180 N strap force supports part of the weight, so the floor carries 720 N rather than 900 N

questions.answer: V = 0.400 × 0.300 × 0.0200 = 2.40 × 10⁻³ m³. m = ρV = 2700 × 2.40 × 10⁻³ = 6.48 kg. The total pad area is 4 × 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ = 2.40 × 10⁻³ m². At equilibrium the floor normal force equals the weight: N = mg = 6.48 × 9.81 = 63.6 N. p = 63.6/(2.40 × 10⁻³) = 2.65 × 10⁴ Pa.
accepted_alternatives: Pressure 26.5 kPa using unrounded intermediate values
questions.unit_policy: Volume must be in m³, mass in kg, total area in m², force in N and pressure in Pa or an exactly equivalent prefixed SI unit.
questions.tolerance: Accept 2.40 × 10⁻³ m³, 6.48 kg, 2.40 × 10⁻³ m², 63.6 N and 2.65 × 10⁴ Pa to three significant figures; allow final pressure from a consistently rounded force.

marking_points.text: Calculates block volume as 2.40 × 10⁻³ m³
Uses m = ρV with density 2700 kg m⁻³
Obtains block mass 6.48 kg
Converts and combines four pad areas to obtain 2.40 × 10⁻³ m²
Uses equilibrium and N = mg to obtain normal force 63.6 N
Uses p = F/A with the normal force and total pad area
Obtains average pressure 2.65 × 10⁴ Pa
